rule: good. the rule line is never parsed; its content reaches the knowledge base through the second sentence, which parses as a clean fireable rule — the first says the same thing but needs the fix noted below.
texts: bad: the slow burning is attached to the batch of mire-essence instead of to the occasion of adding, so two winter additions to the same essence collapse into a single burning recorded as happening during both. The wording is otherwise fine — use the recurring-occasion form that the near-identical second sentence parsed correctly with: "Whenever a Keeper adds salt-bloom to mire-essence in winter, that mire-essence burns slowly."

good. parses as a fireable rule — the winter mixing is the trigger, a slow burning is minted for each such occasion and tied to it, and "that mire-essence" correctly points back to the essence named in the condition.

bad: "cold winds" as a bare plural object gives the translator nowhere to record "cold", and the parse ends up inventing a private cold wind for every salt-bloomed lantern — asserting winds the sentence never says exist. Put the wind in its own condition clause, the shape that parsed cleanly for the cold-wind sentences elsewhere in this batch: "When a cold wind blows against a salt-bloomed lantern, that lantern resists the wind."
